html:
SMTO-SLM-0002 — SMTO couldn't tell which SLURM cluster this is

GUID: 16484db3-aec4-4d18-a3e9-29ee78ff8e44
Slug: slurm-identity-unverified
Domain: SLM · Subsystem: slm

What happened

  • The cluster's settings file doesn't point clearly to one SLURM cluster. Your SLURM command still runs, but SMTO won't remember which cluster this conversation uses.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the administrator to check that slurm.conf names the cluster once (one ClusterName line) and lists at least one scheduler computer (a SlurmctldHost line). SMTO needs both the cluster name and its scheduler computer to recognise the cluster.
  2. If the Gateway computer has both /etc/slurm/slurm.conf and /etc/slurm.conf, ask them to set SLURM_CONF to the real one for the Gateway. With two possible settings files, SMTO can't safely guess which one SLURM is using.
  3. If an Include line in slurm.conf uses %c, ask them to put the ClusterName line above it. The %c in that line is filled in with the cluster name, which must already be known.
  4. After a fix, ask the Agent to run sinfo on that Gateway. A successful simple SLURM read lets SMTO recognise the cluster again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs sinfo or squeue on that Gateway without this error, and later SLURM requests in the conversation use the same cluster.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the SLURM cluster or SMTO. Don't reuse an old cluster choice from before the settings changed; run a fresh SLURM read instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SLURM discovery could not derive one cluster identity: ClusterName or SlurmctldHost is missing, an identity key is duplicated, both /etc/slurm/slurm.conf and /etc/slurm.conf exist without SLURM_CONF, an Include uses %c before ClusterName, or a saved fingerprint/config reference is malformed.

What this means

  • Public identity validation rejects malformed digests/config references, default configuration is ambiguous, or parsing finds missing/duplicate identity keys or unresolved cluster substitution. These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.

Why this can happen

  • Public identity validation rejects malformed digests/config references, default configuration is ambiguous, or parsing finds missing/duplicate identity keys or unresolved cluster substitution.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate malformed saved identity from ambiguous current defaults/includes and missing cluster/controller fields.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, ensure exactly one ClusterName and at least one SlurmctldHost across slurm.conf and its includes, with no repeated ClusterName, SlurmctldAddr or SlurmctldPort. If both /etc/slurm/slurm.conf and /etc/slurm.conf exist, set SLURM_CONF to the real file for the Gateway. Define ClusterName before any Include that uses %c, then rerun a read-only SLURM command to rediscover.
  • Refresh discovery from the intended authoritative SLURM configuration. Resolve duplicate identity keys and ambiguous compiled defaults before using its returned fingerprint.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh supported discovery returns one coherent current configuration identity.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
